### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-mongodb`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **51** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9bff554ef125649be4887880a2e3ac75f14de02b`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 39 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9bff554ef125649be4887880a2e3ac75f14de02b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bd4f5a4aff63dbf8e994733073654745d5ca8151` — the merge of head `0726ee51fb610e682b6f1503117ce4844b9fab3c` into base `9bff554ef125649be4887880a2e3ac75f14de02b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bd4f5a4aff63dbf8e994733073654745d5ca8151 && git checkout bd4f5a4aff63dbf8e994733073654745d5ca8151
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9bff554ef125649be4887880a2e3ac75f14de02b 0726ee51fb610e682b6f1503117ce4844b9fab3c && git checkout -B drift-repro 9bff554ef125649be4887880a2e3ac75f14de02b && git merge --no-ff 0726ee51fb610e682b6f1503117ce4844b9fab3c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9bff554ef125649be4887880a2e3ac75f14de02b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9bff554ef125649be4887880a2e3ac75f14de02b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0726ee51fb610e682b6f1503117ce4844b9fab3c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: only commit 0726ee51 is reviewed (`git diff 79e56778 0726ee51`, 24 files); commit 79e56778 is P1 (PR #32356), reviewed separately and not judged here. Every non-prose path of that diff: packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/user-permission-set-packageless-index.ts (+ .test, .live-postgres.test, .live-mysql.test), activation-ledger-packageless-index.ts, runtime-index-preflight.ts (+ .test), packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts, plugin.ts; packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, index.ts and the four test contexts given a no-op `trigger`; packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-schema.ts, mongodb-user-permission-set-packageless.test.ts; packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-user-permission-set-packageless.test.ts; packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/user-permission-set-guard-at-schema-sync.test.ts; packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/duplicates.contract.test.ts, duplicates.integration.test.ts; packages/types/src/driver-error-classification.callers.test.ts; scripts/check-settings-bind-window.mjs. Prose, judged for accuracy: the changeset and the PR body. + read, not reviewed: packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts at 79e56778 (`isSyncReproducibleIndex`, `isRuntimeManagedIndex`, `parseHashShadowRowScope`, the orphan pass), sql-driver-schema-sync.ts (`rebuildSqliteTablePatched`), packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts and packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts (the `runPlatformMigrations` values), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-user-permission-set.object.ts (the declared key on this head). Not read: partial-index-probe.ts, read-probe.ts, the kernel's `trigger` implementation, and any host outside this repository.

Check-runs on this head (polled once): "every check green" is NOT met. No failure. 34 unfinished (in_progress): Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check UI, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus. 19 green. 13 skipped by job condition, so no verdict here: the Dogfood shards and Dogfood Verify CLI, "Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)" (the only job that runs the live-mysql and live-postgres files), "18.x upgrade harness (opt-in)", Check PR Size, Build Docs, Lint UI, UI Published Artifacts, Packed-tarball smoke, Auto Label, the two queue-verdict jobs and the schedule gate. The PR is a draft; `mergeable_state` is blocked.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Harmless on main + P1 before P2 widens the key: holds, on what the code shows.**
  - The declared key on this head is still `(user_id, permission_set, organization_id)`, `unique: 'organization'`. The guard covers a subset of what it refuses and exempts a NULL organization as it does.
  - The SQL differ offers no orphan drop for the guard. A partial index, the MySQL functional key and the MariaDB row-scoped carrier are all runtime-managed (`isSyncReproducibleIndex` is false for them).
  - On Mongo the `'organization'` unique is outside `retireWidenedUniques`' filter, so nothing is retired. The declared unique and the guard share a key pattern with different partial filters. As I recall MongoDB admits that from 5.0, the driver's stated floor; the documentation pages I fetched did not state it, and nothing was measured.
  - No request's answer moves.
- **The guard, per dialect: the ruled route.** The partial index, the MySQL digest form (NULL when any part is NULL), the MariaDB INVISIBLE carrier named as `hashShadowColumnFor` derives, and the Mongo entry with `permission_set_package: null` are the ledger precedent applied to the grant table.
- **Epic condition 2: met.** Re-runnable on every arm. On duplicates it returns `conflict`, names ten keys then a count, and gives the listing query. No row is deleted or re-stamped.
- **Epic condition 3: met.** The driver-memory admission is measured, pinned and declared.
- **Schema-sync timing (MF6): met on a kernel whose platform-migrations gate is on, not met elsewhere (must-fix 1).**
  - `ObjectQLPlugin` triggers `objectql:schema-synced` at the end of each `syncRegisteredSchemas` pass, inside the boot's schema-migration lock, and the plugin dispatches it, so `bootPhaseHooks: false` does not withhold it.
  - The early returns before the trigger (no engine, no objects) are passes with no DDL.
  - Pinned through a booted kernel on SQLite, with and without `bootPhaseHooks: false`; the ablation is declared red, and I did not re-run it.
- **A dialect with no form keeps the old key: as ruled, and declared.** MySQL before 8.0.13 and MariaDB before 10.3 keep or build `uniq_sys_user_permission_set_ac248331`, pinned equal to driver-sql's `buildIndexName`, with one error line per boot.
- **SF8: closed.**
  - A refused runtime-owned unique gives one error line and the sync goes on, for E11000, 85, 86 and anything else.
  - The legacy-sparse rebuild arm still runs first. A declared index refused with E11000 still fails the sync (CONTROL pinned).
  - The widening arm keeps the old unique because the guard is absent.
  - The pins use a recording Db; the real-mongod suite is opt-in and first runs on `main`.
- **Roster:** `os migrate duplicates` lists six, with the same probe SQL the migration uses; the types and cli roster pins are updated.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on three packages with additive exports (`OBJECTQL_SCHEMA_SYNCED_HOOK`, the migration's functions, constants and types, the optional `SchemaSyncLogger.error`) is the level the prior record read AGENTS as prescribing.
- `Clause-②: no` is right, and line-initial in both bodies. The one FROM→TO line is a loosening of a failure plus a new error line, not a narrowing: an E11000 on a runtime-owned Mongo unique moves from the collection's sync failing to an error line with the sync going on, and 85/86 from silent to an error line. It is stated for both entries, the ledger's included. No capability is taken from a consumer, so no first-party count is owed.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct. The ADR-0087 marker is present and apt.
- The changeset writes "measured" only for SQLite and PG16 and "pinned" for the rest, as should-fix 5 of the prior record asked.
- Undeclared: the `runPlatformMigrations` gate the guard sits behind (must-fix 1).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `os-support-ai`, not `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. Read that before landing.
- **`skipSchemaSync` boots: accepted as declared, with one correction owed.** The changeset says the out-of-band DDL "owns the guard as it owns every table". The repo's own out-of-band DDL (`os migrate apply`, a one-shot boot with `runPlatformMigrations: false`) does not build it, so on such a deployment the guard first appears at `kernel:ready` of a serving boot, and never with `bootPhaseHooks: false`. This folds into must-fix 1.
- **driver-memory exemption: accepted** (condition 3).
- **Live MySQL, MariaDB and mongod unmeasured: accepted as declared.** They first run on `main`.

### ④ Design judgment

**must-fix**
1. **MF6 is not closed on a kernel whose platform-migrations gate is off.**
   - Both the `objectql:schema-synced` subscription and the `kernel:ready` second chance sit inside `if (shouldRunPlatformMigrations(environmentId, options.runPlatformMigrations))` in `metadata-protocol/src/plugin.ts`.
   - The gate is false for any kernel that passes an `environmentId` without declaring `runPlatformMigrations` (the code's own comment: "Cloud passes no value here"), and for every one-shot CLI boot (`schema-migrate.ts` passes `false`, the write modes included).
   - Such a kernel still creates `sys_user_permission_set` at its own schema sync, with its declared indexes, so the old key stood there from the first DDL. The guard never does.
   - Once P2 widens the key, a fresh database on such a host admits every second package-less grant for good. That is the ruling's own case, "every grant on a host that never builds it" (epic 6774878772: on every host, and a declaration is not enough).
   - The gate's two reasons do not transfer as written: the grant table belongs to plugin-security, not to the metadata-storage tables a per-project kernel leaves to the control plane; a read-only one-shot boot must still not write.
   - Nothing in the changeset, the PR body or the module doc mentions the gate, and the MF6 pin boots only an undeclared kernel with no `environmentId`.
   - Do: build the guard on every kernel that runs DDL for the table, keeping the no-write one-shot boots out; or keep the old three-column key where the guard is not built, as the ruling's fallback says. Pin a kernel with an `environmentId` and no declared `runPlatformMigrations`. If the gate is to stay, the epic seat rules it and it is declared.
   - Harmless on P1b alone; it binds before P2 lands.

**should-fix**
2. **The guard is latched for the process once built.** `grantGuardSettled` turns true on `created`, so a later pass does not re-ensure it. `rebuildSqliteTablePatched` drops every index and recreates only the declared ones, so a SQLite table rebuild after the first pass (a later sync pass, or `os migrate apply` beside a running server) leaves the guard absent until the next boot. The statement is `IF NOT EXISTS`; latch only the refusals, so a later pass re-ensures it without reporting a refusal twice.

**nit**
- The unsupported-dialect error line says the old key refuses a second package's set "which the declared key admits". That is false until P2 lands.
- The module doc and the Mongo test header state the four-column key as the declared one. Same cause.
- The Mongo 85/86 line says the key "is NOT enforced … can coexist" and also that the older unique is kept. When the refusal is an older unique on the same key, that key is enforced.
- The cli contract test's title still says "kernel:ready indexes" for a roster whose sixth entry is built at schema sync.

**Tried and held:**
- The drift differ against the guard on each SQL dialect, with the declared key still three columns.
- The MariaDB carrier against the orphan-column pass.
- The Mongo create order: declared indexes first, runtime-owned after, retire last.
- A second boot on each arm (`IF NOT EXISTS`, ER_DUP_KEYNAME, ER_DUP_FIELDNAME then the key).
- The trigger on the `metadata:reloaded` re-sync (a no-op once settled).
- A handler throw (caught inside `ensureGrantGuard`).
- The settings bind-window roster entry.

**Prior record 6774837781:** MF6 (its should-fix 6, raised to must-fix by 6774899763) is closed for the default serving kernel and open as must-fix 1. SF8 is closed. Should-fix 5's wording is corrected in this changeset. Its other items belong to P1 and P2.

Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzeeBmtefMTT21doena`
